claims_disputed.claim: Treating architecture as continuously evolving state rather than a one-shot plan is the source of the gains ('a paradigm shift')
claims_disputed.reason: What was tested is metric-gated refinement of the plan before coding: the architecture is frozen at convergence (§II-D). The size of that effect on statsmodels is +12.0 pp pass in Table III but +3.6 pp in RQ3 (81.90 -> 85.51) for what the text describes as the same 'initial architecture used as fixed' condition. Against RPG, evolution is bundled with the Dual-DAG and requirement context, so 'the source of the gains' is not isolated.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: §III-E: each method only constructs the repository structure, then 'all methods share the same downstream code-generation, validation, and repair scaffold'. mini-SWE-agent is therefore scored as a structure producer feeding Repo0's own TDD pipeline, not as an open coding loop, and its budget is unreported. The paper gives no evidence on a single-agent loop used as the coding harness.

missed_issues: Second internal inconsistency: RQ3 reports statsmodels/GPT-5 mini 'w/o evolution' at coverage 75.90, pass 81.90, voting 93.00 (§IV-C). Table III 'w/o Structural Evolution' for the same repo is 75.35, 73.51 and 93.65. Both are described as using the initial architecture as fixed, and the structural-evolution pass-rate gain is 3.6 pp or 12.0 pp depending on which is believed.

Measured against Table II's django Repo0 coverage (80.50), three of the four Table III ablations have higher django coverage (81.58-83.56). The django coverage deltas therefore change sign depending on which Repo0 row is used, not just in magnitude.

For the DAG-vs-loop question: because the shared scaffold does all coding, the headline comparisons are between planners (structure producers), not between a DAG pipeline and an open agent loop. The large margins over mini-SWE-agent (e.g. 0.00 vs 85.51 pass on statsmodels) measure what structure the loop leaves behind for someone else's TDD scaffold.
RQ3 values for the LLM-decided 1/3/5-round variants appear only in Figure 4, with no numbers in the text, so the size of the deterministic-gate advantage cannot be read from the paper.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats and with the review's P37 and P36 supports, both weak. The ordering ablation and RQ3 are genuine same-model isolating comparisons. I move P10 to neutral because the protocol never runs the plain loop as the coding harness, and I downgrade the 'continuous evolution is the source' claim, since the RQ3 and Table III numbers for the no-evolution condition disagree (3.6 vs 12.0 pp).
